title: Mole Concept & Stoichiometry
syllabus: Matter and its nature, Dalton's atomic theory; Concept of atom, molecule, element, and compound; Laws of chemical combination; Atomic and molecular masses, mole concept, molar mass, percentage composition; Empirical and molecular formulas; Chemical equations and stoichiometry, limiting reagent, sequential and parallel reactions

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An organic compound contains $40\%$ carbon, $6.67\%$ hydrogen, and $53.33\%$ oxygen by mass. If the vapor density of the compound is $30$, its molecular formula is:
questions.solution:
1. Find the mole ratio of the elements:
- Carbon: $\frac{40}{12} = 3.33$
- Hydrogen: $\frac{6.67}{1} = 6.67$
- Oxygen: $\frac{53.33}{16} = 3.33$

2. Simplest whole-number ratio:
$$\text{C} : \text{H} : \text{O} = \frac{3.33}{3.33} : \frac{6.67}{3.33} : \frac{3.33}{3.33} = 1 : 2 : 1$$
Empirical formula = $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$.
Empirical formula mass = $12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30\text{ g/mol}$.

3. Molecular mass $= 2 \times \text{Vapor Density} = 2 \times 30 = 60\text{ g/mol}$.
$$n = \frac{\text{Molecular mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}} = \frac{60}{30} = 2$$
Therefore, Molecular formula = $(\text{CH}_2\text{O})_2 = \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] When $10\text{ g}$ of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) is burnt completely in an excess of oxygen, the volume of $\text{CO}_2$ produced at STP ($22.7\text{ L/mol}$) is approximately:
questions.solution:
The balanced combustion reaction is:
$$\text{CH}_4(g) + 2\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
Molar mass of $\text{CH}_4 = 12 + 4(1) = 16\text{ g/mol}$.
Moles of $\text{CH}_4 = \frac{10}{16} = 0.625\text{ mol}$.

From the stoichiometric coefficients, $1\text{ mol of } \text{CH}_4$ yields $1\text{ mol of } \text{CO}_2$.
Thus, moles of $\text{CO}_2$ formed $= 0.625\text{ mol}$.
$$\text{Volume of } \text{CO}_2 \text{ at STP} = 0.625 \times 22.7 = 14.1875\text{ L} \approx 14.19\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Two oxides of a metal contain $50\%$ and $40\%$ metal by mass respectively. If the formula of the first oxide is $\text{MO}$, the formula of the second oxide is:
questions.solution:
In the first oxide (formula $\text{MO}$):
Metal $= 50\%$, Oxygen $= 50\%$.
$$\frac{\text{Mass of M}}{\text{Mass of O}} = \frac{A_M}{16} = \frac{50}{50} = 1 \implies A_M = 16$$

In the second oxide:
Metal $= 40\%$, Oxygen $= 60\%$.
Ratio of moles of $\text{M}$ to $\text{O}$:
$$\text{Moles of M} = \frac{40}{16} = 2.5$$
$$\text{Moles of O} = \frac{60}{16} = 3.75$$
$$\frac{\text{Moles of M}}{\text{Moles of O}} = \frac{2.5}{3.75} = \frac{2}{3}$$
Wait, if atomic mass is $16$, ratio is $2:3$, which gives $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$ for $40\%$.
Let's verify: for $\text{MO}_2$, Metal $= A_M / (A_M + 32) = 16 / 48 = 33.3\%$.
For $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$, Metal mass $\% = 32 / (32 + 48) = 32/80 = 40\%$.
Thus, formula is $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$ or if first oxide was $\text{M}_2\text{O}$, $A_M = 32$ giving $\text{MO}_2$ for $40\%$.
For this data: $\frac{2.5}{3.75} = \frac{1}{1.5} = \frac{2}{3}$, giving $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following pairs of compounds illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions?
questions.solution:
The Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a ratio of small whole numbers.
- In $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$, Carbon combines with Oxygen.
- In $\text{CO}$, $12\text{ g}$ of carbon combines with $16\text{ g}$ of oxygen.
- In $\text{CO}_2$, $12\text{ g}$ of carbon combines with $32\text{ g}$ of oxygen.
- The mass ratio of oxygen combining with a fixed mass of carbon is $16 : 32 = 1 : 2$, which is a simple whole number ratio.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] $5.6\text{ g}$ of an unknown gas occupies $4.48\text{ L}$ at STP ($0^\circ\text{C}, 1\text{ atm}$, take molar volume $= 22.4\text{ L/mol}$). The gas may be:
questions.solution:
Calculate the number of moles of the gas:
$$n = \frac{\text{Volume at STP}}{\text{Molar volume}} = \frac{4.48\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = 0.2\text{ mol}$$
Molar mass of the gas:
$$M = \frac{\text{Mass}}{n} = \frac{5.6\text{ g}}{0.2\text{ mol}} = 28\text{ g/mol}$$
Comparing molar masses:
- $\text{N}_2: 2 \times 14 = 28\text{ g/mol}$
- $\text{CO}_2: 12 + 32 = 44\text{ g/mol}$
- $\text{O}_2: 2 \times 16 = 32\text{ g/mol}$
- $\text{NO}_2: 14 + 32 = 46\text{ g/mol}$
Hence, the gas is $\text{N}_2$ (or $\text{CO}$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In the reaction $3\text{A} + 2\text{B} \rightarrow \text{A}_3\text{B}_2$, if $5\text{ moles of A}$ and $4\text{ moles of B}$ are reacted, the limiting reagent and the moles of $\text{A}_3\text{B}_2$ formed are:
questions.solution:
Calculate the stoichiometric ratio $\frac{\text{moles}}{\text{stoichiometric coefficient}}$ for each reactant:
- For reactant $\text{A}$: $\frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67$
- For reactant $\text{B}$: $\frac{4}{2} = 2.0$

Since $\frac{5}{3} < \frac{4}{2}$, $\text{A}$ is the limiting reagent.
From stoichiometry, $3\text{ moles of A}$ produce $1\text{ mole of } \text{A}_3\text{B}_2$.
$$\text{Moles of } \text{A}_3\text{B}_2 \text{ formed} = \frac{1}{3} \times 5 = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67\text{ mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A hydrated salt $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$ loses $55.9\%$ of its weight on strong heating to form anhydrous $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$. The value of $x$ is: (Molar mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 = 142\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Mass loss is entirely due to the evaporation of water of crystallization.
Let the mass of $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$ be $M = 142 + 18x$.
Percentage of water lost:
$$\frac{18x}{142 + 18x} \times 100 = 55.9$$
$$1800x = 55.9(142) + 55.9(18x)$$
$$1800x = 7937.8 + 1006.2x$$
$$793.8x = 7937.8 \implies x = 10$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The number of atoms present in $1.6\text{ g}$ of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) is: ($N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
1. Molar mass of $\text{CH}_4 = 12 + 4(1) = 16\text{ g/mol}$.
2. Moles of $\text{CH}_4 = \frac{1.6\text{ g}}{16\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$.
3. Number of molecules of $\text{CH}_4 = 0.1 \times N_A$.
4. Each molecule of $\text{CH}_4$ consists of $1 + 4 = 5\text{ atoms}$.
$$\text{Total atoms} = 5 \times 0.1 \times N_A = 0.5 \times N_A = 0.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.011 \times 10^{23}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] What volume of oxygen gas at STP ($22.4\text{ L/mol}$) is required for the complete combustion of $100\text{ mL}$ of acetylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$)?
questions.solution:
Balanced chemical equation for combustion of acetylene:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2(g) + \frac{5}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
By Gay-Lussac's Law of Combining Volumes, gases react in simple whole-number volume ratios under identical temperature and pressure conditions.
From stoichiometry:
$$1\text{ volume of } \text{C}_2\text{H}_2 \text{ requires } 2.5\text{ volumes of } \text{O}_2$$
$$\text{Volume of } \text{O}_2 = 2.5 \times 100\text{ mL} = 250\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] If the isotopic abundance of boron is $^{10}\text{B} = 20\%$ and $^{11}\text{B} = 80\%$, the average atomic mass of boron is:
questions.solution:
Average atomic mass is the weighted average of the isotopes:
$$\bar{A} = \frac{\sum (\% \text{ abundance} \times \text{isotopic mass})}{100}$$
$$\bar{A} = \frac{20(10) + 80(11)}{100} = \frac{200 + 880}{100} = \frac{1080}{100} = 10.8\text{ u}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A mixture of $2\text{ moles of } \text{H}_2$ and $2\text{ moles of } \text{O}_2$ is ignited to form water. The number of moles of unreacted gas left behind is:
questions.solution:
Balanced chemical reaction:
$$2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
Initial moles: $\text{H}_2 = 2\text{ mol}$, $\text{O}_2 = 2\text{ mol}$.
Stoichiometric coefficients require $2\text{ moles of } \text{H}_2$ for every $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_2$.
- $\text{H}_2$ is completely consumed (limiting reagent).
- Moles of $\text{O}_2$ consumed $= 1\text{ mol}$.
- Moles of $\text{O}_2$ remaining unreacted $= 2 - 1 = 1\text{ mol of } \text{O}_2$.

questions.question: A gaseous hydrocarbon upon combustion gives $0.72\text{ g}$ of water and $3.08\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$. The empirical formula of the hydrocarbon is:
questions.solution:
1. Moles of Carbon:
$$\text{Moles of } \text{CO}_2 = \frac{3.08}{44} = 0.07\text{ mol} \implies \text{Moles of C} = 0.07\text{ mol}$$

2. Moles of Hydrogen:
$$\text{Moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{0.72}{18} = 0.04\text{ mol} \implies \text{Moles of H} = 2 \times 0.04 = 0.08\text{ mol}$$

3. Ratio of C to H:
$$\text{C} : \text{H} = 0.07 : 0.08 = 7 : 8$$
Empirical formula = $\text{C}_7\text{H}_8$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Equal masses of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{O}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$ are taken in a container at the same temperature. The ratio of their number of moles is:
questions.solution:
Let the equal mass taken for each gas be $w\text{ grams}$.
Molar masses:
- $M(\text{H}_2) = 2\text{ g/mol}$
- $M(\text{O}_2) = 32\text{ g/mol}$
- $M(\text{CH}_4) = 16\text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles:
$$n(\text{H}_2) : n(\text{O}_2) : n(\text{CH}_4) = \frac{w}{2} : \frac{w}{32} : \frac{w}{16}$$
Multiply throughout by $\frac{32}{w}$:
$$= 16 : 1 : 2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The percentage of nitrogen in urea ($\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$) is approximately:
questions.solution:
Molecular formula of urea: $\text{CH}_4\text{N}_2\text{O}$.
Molar mass of urea:
$$M = 12 + 4(1) + 2(14) + 16 = 12 + 4 + 28 + 16 = 60\text{ g/mol}$$
Mass of nitrogen in $1\text{ mole of urea} = 2 \times 14 = 28\text{ g}$.
$$\%\text{ of Nitrogen} = \frac{28}{60} \times 100 = 46.666\dots\% \approx 46.7\%$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] $1\text{ L}$ of a gaseous mixture of $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ is passed over red-hot charcoal, and the volume increases to $1.6\text{ L}$ (all volumes measured under identical conditions). The initial volume of $\text{CO}_2$ in the mixture was:
questions.solution:
Let the original volume of $\text{CO}_2$ be $V\text{ L}$.
Then the volume of $\text{CO}$ is $(1 - V)\text{ L}$.
Only $\text{CO}_2$ reacts with charcoal according to the equation:
$$\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{C}(s) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}(g)$$
- $V\text{ L of } \text{CO}_2$ gives $2V\text{ L of } \text{CO}$.
- $\text{CO}$ initially present does not react, remaining $(1 - V)\text{ L}$.
Total final volume:
$$V_{\text{final}} = 2V + (1 - V) = 1 + V$$
Given $V_{\text{final}} = 1.6\text{ L}$:
$$1 + V = 1.6 \implies V = 0.6\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The mass of $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitated when $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M } \text{BaCl}_2$ is mixed with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is: (Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 233.3\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Precipitation reaction:
$$\text{BaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 \downarrow + 2\text{HCl}$$
Calculate millimoles:
- $\text{Millimoles of } \text{BaCl}_2 = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ mmol} = 0.05\text{ mol}$
- $\text{Millimoles of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 100 \times 0.2 = 20\text{ mmol} = 0.02\text{ mol}$

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is the limiting reagent.
Moles of $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitated $= 0.02\text{ mol}$.
$$\text{Mass of } \text{BaSO}_4 = 0.02 \times 233.3 = 4.666\text{ g} \approx 4.67\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An oxide of nitrogen contains $30.43\%$ nitrogen and $69.57\%$ oxygen. Its molecular mass is $92\text{ g/mol}$. The molecular formula is:
questions.solution:
1. Moles of N: $\frac{30.43}{14} = 2.174$
2. Moles of O: $\frac{69.57}{16} = 4.348$
3. Ratio of N to O: $\frac{2.174}{2.174} : \frac{4.348}{2.174} = 1 : 2$
Empirical formula = $\text{NO}_2$.
Empirical formula mass $= 14 + 2(16) = 46\text{ g/mol}$.
$$n = \frac{\text{Molecular mass}}{\text{Empirical mass}} = \frac{92}{46} = 2$$
Therefore, Molecular formula = $(\text{NO}_2)_2 = \text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.

questions.question: Which of the following contains the greatest number of molecules?
questions.solution:
Number of molecules is proportional to the number of moles ($n = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}}$).
For equal mass ($1\text{ g}$), the substance with the lowest molar mass will have the highest number of moles:
- $n(\text{H}_2) = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5\text{ mol}$
- $n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{1}{32} \approx 0.031\text{ mol}$
- $n(\text{N}_2) = \frac{1}{28} \approx 0.036\text{ mol}$
- $n(\text{CH}_4) = \frac{1}{16} \approx 0.0625\text{ mol}$
Thus, $1\text{ g of } \text{H}_2$ contains the greatest number of molecules.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A metal $M$ forms a chloride with $65.5\%$ chlorine by mass. If $100\text{ mL}$ of the vapor of this volatile chloride at STP weighs $0.72\text{ g}$, the molecular formula of the chloride is: (Molar volume $= 22.4\text{ L/mol}$, Atomic mass of $\text{Cl} = 35.5$)
questions.solution:
1. Find molar mass of the chloride:
$$n = \frac{0.1\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = \frac{1}{224}\text{ mol}$$
$$\text{Molar mass } M = \frac{\text{mass}}{n} = 0.72 \times 224 = 161.28\text{ g/mol} \approx 162.5\text{ g/mol}$$
2. Mass of chlorine in one mole:
$$\text{Mass of Cl} = 162.5 \times 0.655 = 106.44\text{ g}$$
$$\text{Number of Cl atoms} = \frac{106.44}{35.5} = 3$$
3. Mass of metal $M = 162.5 - 106.5 = 56\text{ g/mol}$ (which corresponds to Iron, $\text{Fe}$).
Thus, the formula is $\text{FeCl}_3$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When $30\text{ L of } \text{H}_2$ and $30\text{ L of } \text{N}_2$ are reacted under conditions where ammonia is formed with $50\%$ yield, the total volume of the final gaseous mixture is:
questions.solution:
Haber process reaction:
$$\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)$$
For $30\text{ L of } \text{H}_2$, theoretical complete reaction requires $\frac{30}{3} = 10\text{ L of } \text{N}_2$.
Thus, $\text{H}_2$ is the limiting reagent.
At $100\%$ yield:
- $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= 30\text{ L}$
- $\text{N}_2$ consumed $= 10\text{ L}$
- $\text{NH}_3$ produced $= 20\text{ L}$

At $50\%$ yield:
- $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= 0.5 \times 30 = 15\text{ L} \implies \text{remaining } \text{H}_2 = 30 - 15 = 15\text{ L}$
- $\text{N}_2$ consumed $= 0.5 \times 10 = 5\text{ L} \implies \text{remaining } \text{N}_2 = 30 - 5 = 25\text{ L}$
- $\text{NH}_3$ produced $= 0.5 \times 20 = 10\text{ L}$
$$\text{Total final volume} = 15 + 25 + 10 = 50\text{ L}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the mass (in grams) of pure $\text{CaCO}_3$ required to produce $11.2\text{ L}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas at STP ($22.4\text{ L/mol}$) upon complete thermal decomposition.
questions.solution:
Decomposition reaction:
$$\text{CaCO}_3(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$$
Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ required:
$$n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{11.2\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = 0.5\text{ mol}$$
From 1:1 stoichiometry, moles of $\text{CaCO}_3$ required $= 0.5\text{ mol}$.
Molar mass of $\text{CaCO}_3 = 40 + 12 + 3(16) = 100\text{ g/mol}$.
$$\text{Mass of } \text{CaCO}_3 = 0.5 \times 100 = 50.0\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the total number of moles of electrons present in $1.8\text{ g}$ of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2(1) + 16 = 18\text{ g/mol}$.
Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{1.8\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$.
Number of electrons in one molecule of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2(1) + 8 = 10\text{ electrons}$.
Total moles of electrons:
$$\text{Moles of electrons} = 0.1 \times 10 = 1.0\text{ mol}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A sample of $\text{KClO}_3$ on decomposition produces $48\text{ g}$ of oxygen gas. Find the mass (in grams) of potassium chloride ($\text{KCl}$) formed. (Molar mass of $\text{KCl} = 74.5\text{ g/mol}$, $\text{O} = 16\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Balanced chemical equation:
$$2\text{KClO}_3(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{KCl}(s) + 3\text{O}_2(g)$$
Moles of $\text{O}_2$ produced:
$$n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{48\text{ g}}{32\text{ g/mol}} = 1.5\text{ mol}$$
According to the stoichiometry:
$$3\text{ moles of } \text{O}_2 \text{ are produced alongside } 2\text{ moles of } \text{KCl}$$
$$\text{Moles of } \text{KCl} = \frac{2}{3} \times n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{2}{3} \times 1.5 = 1.0\text{ mol}$$
$$\text{Mass of } \text{KCl} = 1.0 \times 74.5 = 74.5\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Complete combustion of $3\text{ g}$ of ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) produces $x\text{ grams}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
Combustion equation:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \frac{7}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Molar mass of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 = 2(12) + 6(1) = 30\text{ g/mol}$.
Moles of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 = \frac{3\text{ g}}{30\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$.
From stoichiometry:
$$\text{Moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 3 \times n(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) = 3 \times 0.1 = 0.3\text{ mol}$$
Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 18\text{ g/mol}$.
$$\text{Mass of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 0.3 \times 18 = 5.4\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In an experiment, $20\text{ g}$ of a metal reacts completely with oxygen to form $28\text{ g}$ of its metal oxide. Find the equivalent mass of the metal.
questions.solution:
Mass of metal $= 20\text{ g}$.
Mass of metal oxide $= 28\text{ g}$.
Mass of combined oxygen $= 28 - 20 = 8\text{ g}$.
By definition, the equivalent mass of an element is the mass that combines with $8\text{ g}$ of oxygen:
$$\text{Equivalent mass of metal} = \frac{\text{Mass of metal}}{\text{Mass of oxygen}} \times 8 = \frac{20}{8} \times 8 = 20.0$$
